questions.title: Which television series will win Outstanding Comedy Series at the 2026 Primetime Emmy Awards?

questions.current_reasoning: Major Bayesian upgrade for Widow's Bay (0.58 -> 0.72) after dominating Night 2 of the 78th Creative Arts Emmys on Sept 6 with 8 wins from 10 nominations (leading all shows across both nights, while Apple TV led all platforms with 19 wins). Crucially, Widow's Bay won Casting for a Comedy Series (beating Hacks, Abbott Elementary, OMITB, Shrinking), Guest Actress in a Comedy Series (Betty Gilpin defeating five separate Hacks nominees plus Jamie Lee Curtis), Cinematography (Half-Hour), Production Design (Half-Hour), Original Dramatic Score, Music Supervision, Sound Editing, and Sound Mixing—winning 5 of 6 direct matchups with Hacks. Its only two losses were Guest Actor (to a poignant posthumous win for Rob Reiner in The Bear) and Single-Camera Picture Editing (where three Widow's Bay episodes likely split votes). Conversely, Hacks went just 1-for-17 on Night 2 (losing Contemporary Costumes, Hair, and Makeup all to Margo's Got Money Troubles, which won 3), though its lone win was Single-Camera Picture Editing for its series finale ('Hacks (Finale)'). Gold Derby's early Sept 7 post-Creative Arts odds already moved to 65.2% Widow's Bay vs 34.8% Hacks (lagging prior real-money market strength). We keep Hacks at 0.255 (down from 0.38) because Hacks historically underperforms at Creative Arts (winning 0 in 2024 before still winning Best Comedy Series), captured Single-Cam Editing for its finale, and rides Jean Smart's 5-for-5 farewell narrative; Margo's Got Money Troubles moves to #3 (0.008) ahead of shut-out Abbott Elementary (0.007) and The Bear (0.006; sum 0.996).

questions.title: Which country will be the first in 2026 to publicly acknowledge deploying purpose-built weapons in Earth orbit?
questions.background: Military satellites provide communications, navigation and intelligence services. Deploying weapons in orbit could significantly change how countries protect or threaten these systems.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Public statements by national governments or military officials, corroborated by reliable international news reporting. Qualifying Event : Resolve to the country whose government or military first publicly acknowledges during 2026 that it has already deployed purpose-built weapons in Earth orbit. Merely describing satellites with potential military applications, announcing future deployments, or confirming ground-based anti-satellite weapons does not qualify. Resolution Timing : Resolve on the date of the first qualifying public acknowledgment, provided it occurs by December 31, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The country's commonly used English name.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-09-06 check (Exa + Sept 2 Reuters/Straits Times investigation 'US, China arm for space warfare: hunter satellites and orbital weapons'): No country has yet publicly acknowledged already-deployed orbital weapons. Crucially, the Sept 2 Reuters report sharpens the asymmetry in public-acknowledgment propensity: China's Foreign Ministry reiterated on the record that Beijing opposes space weaponization and insists its spaceplane/Shiyan missions are peaceful/experimental, and Moscow continues denying its nuclear ASAT program. By contrast, US SPACECOM head Gen. Stephen Whiting is openly arguing for an active warfighting posture and orbital interceptors, incoming Space Force CSO Lt. Gen. Douglas Schiess led the newly disclosed US-UK orbital proximity operation, and the Space Force already broke silence in June with a rare disclosure of an earthbound L3Harris ASAT jammer—building toward potential deterrence disclosures at the mid-September AFA Air, Space & Cyber Conference. Lifting United States (0.49 -> 0.53) while trimming Russia (0.25 -> 0.23) and China (0.12 -> 0.10), with France (0.08, Yoda) and India (0.03) steady (sum = 0.97).

questions.title: Which club will win the 2026 Campeones Cup?
questions.background: The Campeones Cup is an annual match between the previous season’s MLS Cup champion and the winner of Mexico’s Campeón de Campeones.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The official competition result published by Major League Soccer, supported by reliable match reporting. Resolution : Resolve to the club officially declared the winner of the 2026 Campeones Cup once the match has concluded, including extra time or a penalty shootout if required. questions.current_reasoning: Modestly trimming Inter Miami CF (-0.03 to 0.55) and lifting Cruz Azul (+0.03 to 0.45) ahead of the Sept 16 single-leg Campeones Cup final at Nu Stadium following Miami's Sept 5/6 MLS result and a full September schedule comparison. Although Lionel Messi stayed sharp in his first match since retiring from Argentina (2 assists, crossbar free kick) and Casemiro plus Luis Suarez scored, Miami were held 2-2 at home by lowly Atlanta United (6-13-3, 21 pts)—conceding two goals and two penalties (one saved by Dayne St. Clair, one scored by Breel Embolo in the 87') with Casemiro deployed at center-back, leaving Miami with just one win in their last seven MLS matches. Moreover, verified September calendars show Inter Miami face heavier pre-final congestion (4 matches in 11 days: Sept 5 Atlanta after a 90-min lightning delay, Sept 9 away at playoff-contending Chicago Fire, Sept 12 vs Eastern Conference-leading Nashville SC [16-2-4], then Sept 16 Cruz Azul), whereas 10th-placed Cruz Azul (3W-3L, playing winless Santos Laguna tonight Sept 6) have no midweek game before their Sept 12 Clasico Joven vs Liga MX leaders Club America. Miami remain deserved ~55% favorites on home soil with a non-traveling Messi and Cruz Azul's America/travel/Monterrey (Sept 19) rotation dilemma reported by AS Mexico, but 0.55/0.45 better prices Miami's defensive fragility and veteran fatigue.
